 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 17-11-2022 at about 8.00 a.m., the petitioner was going towards Srinivasapura from his village Sonnapalli as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-EB- 8300, ridden by his friend Chowdareddy, slowly, cautiously, on the correct left side of Srinivasapura-Punganur road.

On the way, at Doddabandralahalli Village, Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District, the driver of the school bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-0149 came from opposite direction with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed violently against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, both the occupants of the motorcycle were knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, he was working as mason and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Gownapalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said school bus for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

He has contended that, he is the owner of the bus bearing No.KA-07- 0149 and he has insured his vehicle with the respondent No.2 and he has paid up to date premium to the respondent No.2, the registration certificate and insurance policy continued in his name and as on the date of accident, the policy was in force.
Under the circumstances, he is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

If this Court comes to conclusion that, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner, the liability has to be saddled on the respondent No.2 and it is solely liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to Anjappa vs The Head Master, S.F.S. High School on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171089397/
2 dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: 5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of bus bearing No.KA-07-A-0149 in favour of respondent No.1 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 150(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the involvement of the insured vehicle in the alleged accident.
It has contended that, the rider of the motorcycle was negligent in causing the accident.
The accident took place on 17-11-2022, however the complaint was lodged on 20-11-2022, after lapse of 3 days from the date of alleged accident.
The bus bearing No.KA-07-A-0149 was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the insured and the police to get the compensation from it.

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the offending vehicle was not having valid permit to ply at the place of accident, thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-EB-8300 was also not having valid and effective driving licence to ride the same.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It has also denied the occurrence and mode of the accident and also involvement of the bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-A-0149 as mentioned in the claim petition.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 17-11-2022 at about 8.00 a.m., at Srinivasapura-Punganur Road, Doddabandralahalli Village, Srinivasapura Taluk,
Kolar, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the School bus bearing registration No.KA-07-0149 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.

What order or Award?

Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Srinivas K as P.W.2 and Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as P.W.3 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined the Superintendent of RTO and its Legal Officer as as R.W.1 and R.W.2 respectively and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side.

The respondent No.1 has not Anjappa vs The Head Master, S.F.S. High School on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171089397/

sentences.text: 8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 17-11-2022 at about 8.00 a.m., when the petitioner was going towards Srinivasapura from his village Sonnapalli as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-07-EB- 8300, ridden by his friend Chowdareddy, slowly, on the correct left side of Srinivasapura-Punganur road, at Doddabandralahalli Village, Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District, the driver of the school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07- 0149 came from opposite direction with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed violently against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, both the occupants of the motorcycle were knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as mason and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report,
Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.8 is discharge summary, Ex.P.9 are medical bills (total 20), Ex.P.10 are prescriptions (total 17), Ex.P.11 are medical bills (total 3), Ex.P.12 is authorization letter, Ex.P.13 is admission record, Ex.P.14 is clinical notes, Ex.P.15 is x-ray and Ex.P.16 is true copy of MLC register extract.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his right leg.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149.

sentences.text:
At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.
Further, though the respondent No.1 has denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident, he has not specifically denied the involvement of offending bus in the said accident.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle, the offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and same has been falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the insured and the police to claim compensation from it.
But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have failed to establish the said contentions.
The respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on his behalf.
The respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Officer in order to establish the said contentions.

But, except the self serving statements of the representative/Legal Officer of the respondent No.2 insurance company, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle and the offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and same has been falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the insured and the police to claim compensation from it.
On the other hand, the oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated by the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus.
Though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made in his cross- examination that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-EB-8300, the injuries are not caused in the alleged accident and he has lodged a false complaint against the driver of bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149, in collusion with the respondent No.1 and the jurisdictional police.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, as per Ex.P.4 Motor Vehicle Accident report, the front bumper at right side of the offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 is damaged.
If really as contended by the respondent No.2, the said bus was not at all involved in the accident, the immediate question that arises is, how the front portion of the said vehicle has got damaged.
No explanation or justification with respect to same is forthcoming in the evidence of R.W.2.
It is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the said damage was already existing before the date of accident in question in the instant case or the same was caused in some other accident.
This clearly goes to show that, the above contentions of the respondent No.2 are false and imaginary.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on extreme left side of BC road-Doddabindarlahalli road, near Doddabindarlahalli Village,
Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District, due to dashing of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 to the motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which are marked as Ex.P.4, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the Anjappa vs The Head Master, S.F.S. High School on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171089397/
5 motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus.

sentences.text: There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to negligence of the rider of the motorcycle or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-0149.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
Ex.P.13 admission record, Ex.P.14 clinical notes, Ex.P.15 x-ray and Ex.P.16 MLC register extract, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered comminuted fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
The same is deposed by P.W.3, who is the doctor, who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.1 and 2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, with regard to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149.
16.
No doubt, in the present case there is a delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the said delay is properly explained and justified by the complainant.

It is clearly stated in the Ex.P.1 F.I.R., and Ex.P.2 first information statement/complaint that, as the complainant was along with his father to provide treatment to him, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
The medical records clearly reveals that, the petitioner has taken treatment as an in-patient from 17-11-2022 to 23-11- 2022.
This clearly goes to show that, the reason for delay in lodging the complaint stated in the Ex.P.1 F.I.R., and Ex.P2 complaint are true.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint is properly explained and justified by the complainant and there are reasonable grounds to condone the said delay.
Hence, the delay caused in lodging the complaint is not fatal to the present case of the petitioner.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

19. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 17-11-2022 at about 8.00 a.m., on BC road-Doddabindarlahalli road, near Doddabindarlahalli Village, Srinivasapura Taluk,
Kolar District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending school bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-0149.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 and he has sustained comminuted fracture shaft of right femur.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1960.
The accident has taken place on 17-11-2022 at about 8.00 A.M. Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 63 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has treated and examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of his disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered comminuted fracture shaft of right femur.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered 47% physical disability to his right lower limb and 16% to the whole body.

Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate,
Ex.P.8 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 admission record, Ex.P.14 clinical notes, Ex.P.15 x-ray and Ex.P.16 MLC register extract clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered above stated grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made in his cross-examination that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability as stated him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the Anjappa vs The Head Master, S.F.S. 7 petitioner.

sentences.text:
But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 17-11-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 15-05-2024,
which is after lapse of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture sustained by the petitioner is united and the ankle movement and power of the right upper limb are normal.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as mason and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as mason and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Therefore, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 63 years is 7.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 10/100 X 7 = Rs.1,30,200/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 29 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9 and 11.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,10,406/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,10,406/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
comminuted fracture shaft of right femur.
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days from 17-11-2022 to 23-11-2022, in Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar.

In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner,

The petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days as in-patient at Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar, for the grievous injuries sustained in the said accident He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 63 years and unfortunately he has suffered comminuted fracture shaft of right femur.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and the estimate cost of said surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued the estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

21. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 1,30,200-00 2.

9 4. Attendant charges 7,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 5,600-00 6. Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,69,206/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
23.

But, the respondent No.2 insurance company has taken specific contentions in its written statement that, as on the date of accident the driver of the offending bus was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the said bus was not having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.
As there is breach of conditions of the policy, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.1 to prove that, at the of accident his driver was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-0149 and his vehicle was having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.
But, the respondent No.1 has failed to discharge his burden in the case.

The respondent No.1 has neither stepped into witness box to adduce his evidence, nor he has produced any document to show that, at the of accident his driver was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-0149 and his vehicle was having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.
On the other hand, in order to establish the said contentions, the respondent No.2 has examined the Superintendent of RTO, Kolar as R.W.1.

The R.W.1 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the permit issued by his office with respect of bus bearing No.KA-07-A-0149 was valid from 01-02-2023 to 31-01-2028 and as on 17-11-2022 the said permit was not in force.
He has also produced true copy of permit with fee details of bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 07-A-0149, which is marked as Ex.R.2.
As per Ex.R.2 Permit, as on the date of accident the offending bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-A-0149 was not having valid permit to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident.

Further, the evidence of R.W.1, who is Superintendent, RTO Office, Kolar and the document got marked by him as Ex.R.2 clearly establishes that, the permit issued in respect of offending bus bearing No.KA-07-A-0149 was valid from 01-02-2023 to 31-01-2028 and as on the date of accident i.e. 17-11-2022 the said permit was not in force.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further, as the accident in question has taken place after the date of coming into force of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner that, even if there is a fundamental breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act the insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the third party and recover the same from the insured, does not hold good.

Further, the ratio laid down and the observations made in the above cited judgments relied by the learned counsel for petitioner, are not applicable to the present facts and circumstances of the case.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, there is breach of fundamental conditions of the Ex.R.4 insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1 in respect to offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-A-0149 and hence, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Accordingly,
holding that the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation amount Rs.3,69,206/- to the petitioner, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,69,206/- (Rupees three lakh sixty nine thousand two hundred and six only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
The petition against respondent No.2 is dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
